text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but that modest gain masks a steep two-week decline of nearly 10% that accelerated after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The earnings announcement itself doesn't appear to have triggered sudden selling, but the stock has continued falling steadily since then—dropping another 1.5% on November 5th and 6th combined—suggesting investors may have found the results or guidance disappointing relative to expectations, or that the market is repricing oil majors downward for other reasons.

The broader headwind is clearer: oil prices have weakened substantially over the past two weeks. U.S. crude has fallen to $99.64 per barrel, and the price gap between U.S. and world oil has narrowed, which typically signals softer energy demand or growing supply concerns. At the same time, the Democratic sweep in midterm elections has raised investor focus on renewable energy policy and a potential shift away from fossil fuels—a structural concern for oil and gas producers that can weigh on valuations even when commodity prices hold steady.
